opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Santos (employee ID E050) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E050.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Santos (E050) is a full_time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, which is owned by the Engineer role. Full-time employees may have up to write, and admin is permissible only when the role owns the system; requested write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E050 (Jacob Santos) is a contractor with basic security training, so max access is read (write requires advanced training). Requested write is above max; recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent's note (from the Security DB) identifies E050 as a contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors may have at most read unless they have advanced security training (write), and never admin. The requested write is above the maximum of read, so I grant the maximum of read. Note: the HR note lists E050 as full-time (which would permit write), conflicting with the Security DB; the Security DB is the authoritative source for access-level decisions, so I grant read.
